title: Desarmadero La Torre
description: A searchable parts catalog, followed by a returning-client engagement that turned one discovery call into a PRD, spec, and clickable operations prototype.
role: Product direction, specification, and prototype delivery
constraints: Inventory changed constantly, so staff needed a simple way to keep listings current.
Customers needed to find relevant stock without calling the shop first.
The prototype needed to prove understanding before scope and pricing decisions.
problem: A large, changing auto-parts inventory forced customers to call or visit to check stock. After the searchable catalog launched, the same client returned wanting to run the auto-dismantling yard itself. Its operating model was spread across paper sheets, WhatsApp, Excel, and memory.
solution: Built a searchable customer-facing catalog first, then turned one discovery call into a PRD, functional spec, and role-based SvelteKit prototype. The client could click through it before committing to the full build.
result: Customers can search the catalog before calling, turning vague stock questions into more specific inquiries and giving the business a 24/7 stockroom.
The client could validate the operating model through a working prototype instead of abstract requirements, then decide the next scope from concrete evidence.
deliveryHighlights: Searchable catalog by make, model, and year with photos and a direct inquiry path.
A live role-based prototype covering counter sales, cash-desk release, dismantle assignment, yard-map search, and a mobile dismantler view.
PRD, functional spec, discovery transcript, seeded demo, and prototype screenshots as an open work sample.
